# SimJury complete public-site guide

This document describes the public routes and Court Week phases without
disclosing case-specific evidence, juror state, outcomes or analysis.

## Product

SimJury's only case is the fictional **Eleven Minutes**. The player serves as a
juror through five sequential court sessions, then deliberates on Saturday and
Sunday with eleven authored jurors. Each session is self-paced and lasts only as
long as its reviewed dialogue and meaningful juror decisions require. Possible
results are Murder, manslaughter by criminal negligence, Not Guilty, or unable
to agree. The site never declares one outcome objectively correct.

## Canonical public routes

### https://simjury.com/

The static JavaScript player presents, in lawful order: empanelment and oath;
preliminary directions; Crown opening and evidence; defence opening and
evidence; Crown and defence closings; judicial summing-up; retirement; sealed
player ballot; anonymous aggregate ballot; evidence-first deliberation; jury
note and answer; any delayed majority direction; and open-court verdict return.

The experience is audio-first with optional two-line captions and a complete
reading mode. It supports keyboard and touch, reduced motion, visible focus,
screen readers, 200% zoom, phone portrait/landscape, tablet split-screen and
desktop layouts. No orientation, dragging or native-fullscreen capability is
required.

### https://simjury.com/privacy/

The privacy page explains local IndexedDB state, explicit export/import, GitHub
media-request metadata, Cloudflare static-delivery metadata, and the absence of
accounts, server-side analytics, runtime AI and backend player state. Masked
client-side Microsoft Clarity analytics is enabled by default. It may observe
control interaction, including ballot-control timing and sequence, but does not
receive the stored ballot choice, progress, private notes or free-text reasoning.
The privacy page provides a browser-local opt-out.

## Discovery and HTTP behavior

- `robots.txt` permits public assistant/search fetchers, excludes known
  model-training crawlers, and prevents ordinary indexing of hashed app assets.
- Static responses publish `Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes,
  ai-train=no, use=reference` and strict security headers.
- `sitemap.xml` lists `/` and `/privacy/` only.
- `/jury/`, `/today/`, `/play/` and `/install/` redirect to `/`.
- Unknown routes return a real 404 response.

## Architecture and cost boundary

GitHub stores reviewed source and runs trusted batch media/QA workflows. Heavy
media is content-addressed and pinned to one explicit GitHub Release tag.
Cloudflare serves Static Assets only: no Worker, Worker-first route, D1, Durable
Object, KV, R2, Queue, AI, WebSocket, rate limiter, variable, observability or
dynamic rendering. Progress, notes and ballots remain local.
The sole analytics exception is the default-on, fully masked client-side Clarity
tag disclosed above; advertising storage is denied and opting out clears its
cookies and prevents the tag loading on later SimJury pages in that browser.

## Spoiler and publication boundary

This guide intentionally excludes the case title's factual premise, testimony,
exhibit contents, legal analysis, juror rules, hidden positions and verdict
paths. Future session packs and media mappings are not linked by crawl guides.
The archived Daily Docket corpus is outside the public build.
